Job Description The Infrastructure Control Governance (ICG) Sr. Manager is responsible for supporting the ICG (APAC) Director in operating the ICG function. This includes support of the Continuous Control Monitoring, Infrastructure Controls, Vulnerability Oversight, Issue Remediation Oversight, Audit Prep and Access Management oversight domains. JOB RESPONSIBILITIES This role ensures effective governance of the ICG domains (Continuous Control Monitoring, Infrastructure Controls, Vulnerability Oversight, Issue Remediation Oversight, Audit Prep and Access Management) in support of the ICG Director. Specifically, responsibilities include ensuring standardized, centralized and audit-ready control documentation; design and implementation support for automated/AI driven control governance, and help establish governance guardrails for responsible AI usage in control lifecycle management. The role also requires the ability to strengthen compliance posture, while effectively supporting enterprise risk and regulatory objectives. Program Leadership & ICG Governance Support end-to-end execution of ICG functions aligned with Enterprise risk and compliance frameworks. Support program vision, scaling, governance maturity across ICG domains Establish and maintain standardized process, risk and control frameworks (design, taxonomy, ownership, lifecycle). Manage centralized process, risk and control inventory with audit traceability. Control Documentation Standardize and centralize control documentation (objective, procedure, frequency, evidence, ownership) while ensuring version-control and audit-readiness. Ability to utilize AI solutions to help generate and refine control narratives and SOPs, perform consistency validation across control library, and map controls to regulatory frameworks (SOX, NIST, FFIEC) Control Automation/AI & Control Monitoring Design and govern Control Monitoring dashboards which utilize Key Control Indicators (KCIs) and Control Indicators (CIs). Enable AI-driven monitoring to identify anomalies and control failures, predict control breakdown trends, and trigger proactive alerts and remediation Oversee control onboarding lifecycle including feasibility, UAT, and deployment. AI Governance & Guardrails Help ICG Director to define and implement AI guardrails which may include data privacy and secure usage controls, approved use cases for AI in control lifecycle, and validation mechanisms to mitigate AI inaccuracies Develop method to ensure human-in-the-loop validation and auditability of AI outputs. Stakeholder Management Act as liaison across infrastructure teams to ensure risk and compliance objectives are met. Lead governance forums and stakeholder reviews. Partner with control owners and SMEs for control onboarding and remediation tracking. Technical & Data Oversight Oversee integration of data sources ensuring data quality and lineage. Guide development of dashboards and automation solutions (e.g., Power BI, Service Now). Govern UAT and deployment of monitoring solutions. Ensure that Northern Trust or its clients are not exposed to inappropriate or excessive risk. Escalate any risk concerns, including those resulting from mistakes / errors to a manager or business unit risk officer. Exercise diligence regarding cyber-security. Cooperate with internal control functions (including first-line Control, Risk, Compliance, Audit, self-assigned, etc.) and applicable regulatory bodies. Strong stakeholder management and executive communication skills. Good to Have: Experience in Infrastructure Control design and standardization. Exposure to AI governance / Responsible AI frameworks. Experience with predictive analytics or anomaly detection models. Strong program and transformation leadership capabilities. Exposure to regulatory audits and sample-based testing processes. title: Senior Analyst, Credit Analysis & Underwriting - Bangalore
jobDescription:
About Northern Trust As a global leader in innovative wealth management, asset servicing, asset management and banking services, Northern Trust (Nasdaq: NTRS) is proud to guide the world’s most successful individuals, families, corporations and institutions. Since 1889, we have aligned our efforts with our three guiding Principles That Endure: Service, Expertise, and Integrity. Together, they reflect the three cornerstones of business conduct which we strive to instill in our employees, whom we call partners, and to provide to our clients and the communities we serve worldwide. With more than 135 years of financial experience and over 24,000 partners, we serve the world’s most sophisticated clients using leading technology and exceptional service. Job Summary: Under general supervision (while working independently most of the time), the Senior Analyst – Credit Risk in Wealth Management is responsible for conducting in-depth credit analysis of high-net-worth individuals (HNWIs), privately held businesses, not-for-profit organizations, and commercial real estate clients. The Senior Analyst will analyze financial data using tools such as Moody’s Credit Lens, assess creditworthiness, and develop credit analysis reports to support underwriting and lending decisions. In this role, the Senior Analyst manages complex credit analysis assignments, mentors junior analysts, and ensures the accuracy and quality of credit spreads. The Senior Analyst also works on strategic and special projects identified by management. Collaboration with relationship managers and internal stakeholders is required to structure credit facilities that align with clients’ wealth management goals while adhering to Northern Trust’s risk management. This position offers exposure to sophisticated financial products, a dynamic work environment, and opportunities to develop expertise in credit analysis for the wealth management sector. Major Duties: • Analyzes financial statements, credit reports, and economic data to assess the creditworthiness of individuals or businesses. • Prepares comprehensive credit reports with a high degree of independence, focusing on operational performance, financial health, and identification of key risk mitigants. • Monitors borrower performance and ensures timely identification of potential risks by conducting thorough annual reviews. • Mentors junior analysts to ensure adherence to established standards and guidelines. • Contributes to division-wide initiatives and special projects as assigned by management. • Collaborates with onshore partners and relationship managers to develop tailored credit solutions. • Ensures adherence to Northern Trust’s credit policies, compliance standards, process-related guidelines, and controls. • Consistently adheres to established QUALITY & QUANTITY SLAs. • Stays informed about market trends, regulatory changes, and economic factors affecting credit risk. • Pays attention to detail to ensure all documents are processed correctly. • Identifies process changes to improve productivity and efficiency.

QUALIFICATIONS:
• Graduation or above degree in finance, accounting, or business administration (or equivalent) • Additional certifications such as CFA, FRM, CMA, etc., are considered advantageous but are not mandatory. Experience & Skills: • 2
- 4 years of experience in financial spreading and credit memo underwriting, strong financial analysis and analytical skills. Familiarity with lending products such as lines of credit and term loans is required. • Excellent time management skills, with the ability to multitask, work independently, and handle competing priorities under pressure. • Ability to present information in a clear and concise manner, effectively telling the story behind financials in a compelling way. • Ability to research issues/problems and provide a ‘solution-based’ approach • Excellent verbal and written communication and partnering skills. A confident and personable attitude with the ability to communicate effectively with onshore relationship managers and other stakeholders • Self-motivated individual to go beyond immediate responsibilities • Familiarity with Moody’s Credit Lens or similar credit spreading tools. Proficiency in MS Excel and MS Word and other Microsoft 365 tools. • Capability to coach and mentor junior team members. Shift Coverage: EMEA
- 12:30PM to 9:30PM IST About the Team This position is within the Financial Risk Division, organizationally aligned under Global Risk. The department plays a pivotal role in the credit underwriting process, monitoring loans, assessing risks across credit portfolios thereby safeguarding the organization’s financial stability by ensuring rigorous credit analysis, adherence to regulatory standards, and the implementation of robust risk mitigation strategies. Operational Resilience Senior Consultant (P3) – Resilience Pillars Integration Enterprise Resiliency Office (ERO) Location: India (Pune) Role / Department The Operational Resilience Senior Consultant (P3) – Resilience Pillars Integration is a First Line of Defence role within the Enterprise Resiliency Office. The role supports the Operational Resilience and Business Continuity frameworks by working with key stakeholders across core resilience pillars to help ensure consistent, risk‑based resilience requirements are defined, embedded, and monitored across the organisation. The role sits within a dedicated Pillars Integration pod, working globally alongside two other partners to support the integration of resilience requirements across the following pillars: People Premises Technology (including End User Computing and Cyber) Third Party Data The Senior Consultant will partner with pillar owners, change management teams, and other stakeholders to support resilience outcomes, improve visibility of dependencies supporting Important Business Services (IBSs) and Important Internal Services (IISs), and assist in supporting compliance with Operational Resilience and Business Continuity requirements. The role is expected to operate with a level of responsibility appropriate to P3 seniority, contributing to defined workstreams, engaging stakeholders, and developing subject matter expertise while working collaboratively with other partners within the Pillars Integration pod. Key Responsibilities of the Role Support collaboration with global pillar stakeholders to define, agree, and embed minimum resilience requirements aligned to Operational Resilience and Business Continuity frameworks across People, Premises, Technology, Third Party, and Data pillars. Act as a contributing member of the Pillars Integration pod, supporting the delivery of a consistent and coordinated approach to pillar integration globally. Assist in the identification, prioritisation, and tracking of resilience dependencies that support IBSs and IISs, ensuring alignment between pillar‑level activities and enterprise resilience objectives. Support the development and maintenance of processes for obtaining, maintaining, and monitoring data required to assess conformance with resilience requirements at an individual component level. Work with Change Management and relevant stakeholders to support the integration of resilience requirements into change processes, including identifying changes impacting IBSs and IISs. Contribute to the integration of pillar resilience data into enterprise tooling solutions (e.g. Fusion or successor tools), working with internal teams as required. Support the preparation of management information, reporting, and analysis relating to resilience risks, vulnerabilities, and areas of non‑conformance. Monitor and analyse the impact of organisational, process, technology, and third‑party changes on resilience requirements, escalating risks and issues where appropriate. Assist in supporting oversight activities relating to compliance with Operational Resilience policies, standards, and regulatory expectations. Deliver defined tasks and workstream activities within agreed timelines, escalating issues and dependencies as appropriate. Contribute to knowledge sharing within the team and continue to build expertise across resilience pillars.
